plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that follow the sun across the sky. In mid-August, fields across the American Great Plains glow with rows of yellow blooms. Bees and goldfinches crowd the flower heads.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Great Plains and Midwest, United States (also widely grown across Europe and Central Asia)
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is a cluster of hundreds or even thousands of tiny florets, and they are arranged in spirals that follow the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant mounds send up slender spikes of violet-blue flowers that hum with pollinators. In August, the lavender fields of Provence in southern France are in late bloom, and the warm air smells sweet and herbal.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (typically June to August in southern Europe)
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean regions of Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since ancient times, and the plant's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: Tall spires of bright magenta-pink flowers blaze across alpine meadows and burned or cleared land. The blooms open from the bottom of the spike upward through the summer, and by mid-August the spikes are nearing their tops. Fireweed is often among the first plants to recolonize land after a wildfire.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (typically July to September)
plants.location: Alaska, western Canada and the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: Fireweed flowers open from the bottom of the spike to the top. Folk wisdom in Alaska holds that summer is nearly over when the top blossoms open.
